title: The End of the Pandemic Emergency in the U.S.

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The Biden administration said this week it would end the public health emergency for COVID, closing this chapter of the pandemic three years after it started.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府本周表示，将结束针对新冠疫情的公共卫生紧急状态，在疫情开始三年后，翻开这一篇章。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Apoorva Mandevili explains how it will affect Americans and why it does not mean the end of COVID.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事阿普尔瓦·曼德维利将解释这将如何影响美国人，以及为什么这并不意味着新冠疫情的终结。

sentences.en: It's Friday, February 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月3日，星期五。

sentences.en: So Apoorva, the Biden administration announced that the public health emergency around COVID is ending.
sentences.zh: 那么阿普尔瓦，拜登政府宣布围绕新冠疫情的公共卫生紧急状态即将结束。

sentences.en: Can you explain what that means?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so almost exactly three years ago when the pandemic started on January 31St.
sentences.zh: 是的，几乎就在三年前，也就是1月31日疫情开始的时候。

sentences.en: Well, good afternoon, everyone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大家下午好。

sentences.en: I have today declared that the coronavirus presents a public health emergency in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我今天宣布，冠状病毒在美国构成公共卫生紧急状态。

sentences.en: Alex Azar, who was then the Secretary of Health and Human Services, said that we were now in a public health emergency.
sentences.zh: 时任卫生与公众服务部部长的亚历克斯·阿扎尔表示，我们现在处于公共卫生紧急状态中。

sentences.en: In accordance with the declaration,
sentences.zh: 根据该声明，

sentences.en: the United States government will implement temporary measures to increase our abilities to detect and contain the coronavirus proactively and aggressively.
sentences.zh: 美国政府将采取临时措施，以主动且积极地提高我们检测和遏制冠状病毒的能力。

sentences.en: And that was an acknowledgement that the virus was spreading in the country and a public health emergency,
sentences.zh: 那是一次承认病毒正在国内传播，并宣布进入公共卫生紧急状态，

sentences.en: which is something that the government does every once in a while when there is one, allows the government to do a lot of different things to cope with this special situation.
sentences.zh: 这是政府在出现紧急情况时偶尔会做的事情，它允许政府采取许多不同的手段来应对这种特殊情况。

sentences.en: And since January 2020, this public health emergency has been renewed every 90 days.
sentences.zh: 自2020年1月以来，这项公共卫生紧急状态每90天就会续期一次。

sentences.en: But now the Biden administration is saying that that emergency is over and that all of those special things that we did will end on May 11th.
sentences.zh: 但现在拜登政府表示，紧急状态已经结束，我们所采取的所有那些特殊措施都将在5月11日终止。

sentences.en: So the Biden administration is basically letting this declaration of a health emergency expire, right?
sentences.zh: 所以拜登政府基本上是让这项卫生紧急状态声明到期失效，对吧？

sentences.en: But what exactly had this declaration been allowing?
sentences.zh: 但这项声明到底允许了什么？

sentences.en: Like, how have we been seeing it play out in our everyday lives?
sentences.zh: 我们是如何在日常生活中感受到它的作用的？

sentences.en: And for the average person, what it did, most importantly, is it gave us access to free tests, free treatments, free vaccines.
sentences.zh: 对于普通人来说，它最重要的一点是，让我们能够获得免费的检测、免费的治疗和免费的疫苗。

sentences.en: It allowed states, hospitals, nursing homes, various parts of the federal government to deal with COVID outside of the usual framework.
sentences.zh: 它允许各州、医院、疗养院以及联邦政府的各个部门在常规框架之外处理新冠疫情。

sentences.en: It also gave them extra money.
sentences.zh: 它还为他们提供了额外的资金。

sentences.en: And Medicare and other group health plans were covering out of network as if it were in network.
sentences.zh: 而且医疗保险（Medicare）和其他团体健康计划将网络外医疗费用视同网络内进行报销。

sentences.en: Meaning?
sentences.zh: 意思是？

sentences.en: Meaning you could go to any doctor and be treated and you would be treated for free.
sentences.zh: 意思是你可以去看任何医生并接受治疗，而且是免费的。

sentences.en: And the federal government barred states from kicking anybody off of Medicaid for the rest of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府还禁止各州在疫情期间将任何人踢出医疗补助计划（Medicaid）。

sentences.en: I mean, it basically gave the federal government extra muscle to deal with a disaster that was unfolding all around us, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它基本上给了联邦政府额外的力量来应对我们周围正在发生的灾难，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, lessening all the friction in the system so that we could all get care more easily.
sentences.zh: 就像减少系统中的所有摩擦，让我们都能更容易地获得护理。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it gave a lot of extra money and people power.
sentences.zh: 是的，它提供了大量的额外资金和人力。

sentences.en: And it made it possible for private entities and government entities to really fight the pandemic on every front.
sentences.zh: 它使私营实体和政府实体能够真正从各个方面抗击疫情。

sentences.en: And now that's all going away.
sentences.zh: 而现在这一切都要结束了。

sentences.en: It's not all going away, but yes, some of it is going away as of May 11th.
sentences.zh: 并不是全部结束，但确实，从5月11日起，其中一部分将要结束。

sentences.en: And Apoorva, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那么阿普尔瓦，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: Lay this out for me.
sentences.zh: 给我理一理。

sentences.en: What does it mean that it's going away?
sentences.zh: 它要结束了到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means three big things, really.
sentences.zh: 其实意味着三件大事。

sentences.en: Well, the first thing is that the health care system is now going to treat COVID like it's any other disease, like it's diabetes.
sentences.zh: 首先，医疗保健系统现在将把新冠视为任何其他疾病来对待，就像对待糖尿病一样。

sentences.en: So basically it puts COVID into the category of all other health issues.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，它把新冠归入了所有其他健康问题的类别中。

sentences.en: And that means into the category of complicated, right?
sentences.zh: 那也就意味着归入了“复杂”的类别，对吧？

sentences.en: That is the American health care system.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国医疗保健系统。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's incredibly complicated and it will make your head hurt to figure out what you qualify for and what you don't.
sentences.zh: 它极其复杂，弄清楚你符合什么条件、不符合什么条件会让你头疼。

sentences.en: And a lot depends on what kind of insurance you have, like it does for everything else.
sentences.zh: 而且很大程度上取决于你有什么样的保险，就像其他所有事情一样。

sentences.en: If you have private insurance, you may not even notice a difference.
sentences.zh: 如果你有私人保险，你甚至可能感觉不到什么区别。

sentences.en: So if you want a test, if you want a PCR test for COVID, you have to go to the doctor and have them prescribe the teSt.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想要检测，如果你想要进行新冠PCR检测，你必须去看医生，让他们开具检测单。

sentences.en: You can still go to the store and get an antigen test, but you just won't get those eight free tests a month like we were getting.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以去商店买抗原检测试剂盒，但你不会再像以前那样每月获得那八次免费检测了。

sentences.en: If you want a drug, the doctor has to prescribe it for you and your insurance company has to cover it.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要药物，医生必须为你开处方，而且你的保险公司必须承保。

sentences.en: If you have Medicare, you may still be able to get free tests and free treatments, but only if they're ordered by a physician and you may still have out-of-pocket costs.
sentences.zh: 如果你有医疗保险（Medicare），你可能仍然可以获得免费检测和免费治疗，但前提是必须由医生下令，而且你可能仍需承担自付费用。

sentences.en: If you have Medicaid, the tests will only be free till the second half of 2024.
sentences.zh: 如果你有医疗补助（Medicaid），检测免费政策只会持续到2024年下半年。

sentences.en: And Medicaid may even cover drugs like Paxlovid that are under emergency use authorization, but that will depend on your state.
sentences.zh: 医疗补助甚至可能覆盖像Paxlovid这样处于紧急使用授权下的药物，但这取决于你所在的州。

sentences.en: But if you're uninsured, you're not going to be able to get the vaccines, tests, and treatments for free the way that you used to.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有保险，你将无法像以前那样免费获得疫苗、检测和治疗。

sentences.en: You may still be able to get some of them through community clinics, and there are programs to help uninsured children get what they need.
sentences.zh: 你或许还能通过社区诊所获得其中一些服务，也有一些项目可以帮助无保险的儿童获得他们所需的东西。

sentences.en: But if you don't have insurance, you might very well end up paying a lot of money out of pocket for all of this.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有保险，你很可能最终要为这一切支付大笔的自付费用。

sentences.en: And what effect do you think that will have?
sentences.zh: 你认为这会产生什么影响？

sentences.en: I mean, that uninsured people won't have free access to tests and treatments.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有保险的人将无法免费获得检测和治疗。

sentences.en: And it means a lot fewer people will get tested, even fewer than now.
sentences.zh: 这意味着接受检测的人会少得多，甚至比现在还要少。

sentences.en: It means a lot more people will probably get sick because they won't get treated.
sentences.zh: 这意味着可能会有更多人因为得不到治疗而生病。

sentences.en: It means the hospitals may be more full with people who are low income, who've been the hardest hit by the pandemic and will continue to be.
sentences.zh: 这意味着医院里可能会挤满低收入人群，他们是受疫情打击最严重的人，而且未来仍将如此。

sentences.en: And a lot more people will be in that category now because, remember, the federal government allowed states to get extra money in exchange for not booting people off Medicaid?
sentences.zh: 而且现在会有更多人被归入这一类，因为请记住，联邦政府允许各州获得额外资金，条件是不能将人们踢出医疗补助计划。

sentences.en: Well, in December, Congress decided that that should end in April.
sentences.zh: 嗯，去年12月，国会决定这项政策应在4月结束。

sentences.en: And so starting in April, the states are going to start kicking people off of Medicaid and all those people will lose insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以从4月开始，各州将开始把人们踢出医疗补助计划，所有这些人都会失去保险。

sentences.en: And that means a lot of people who are getting all of these things, tests and treatments and vaccines through Medicaid, will now lose them.
sentences.zh: 这意味着许多通过医疗补助获得这些服务——检测、治疗和疫苗——的人现在将失去它们。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: So how many people, roughly, are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 那么我们大概在说多少人？

sentences.en: At the moment, there are about 80 to 90 million people on these total.
sentences.zh: 目前，总共有大约8000万到9000万人享受这些服务。

sentences.en: And there's one estimate that says 15 million may lose it.
sentences.zh: 有一项估计称，可能有1500万人会失去它。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 那可是很多人。

sentences.en: That is a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 确实是很多人。

sentences.en: I mean, we already have about 30 million people in this country who don't have insurance.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们国家已经有大约3000万人没有保险了。

sentences.en: And when people start getting kicked off Medicaid, they will add to those numbers.
sentences.zh: 当人们开始被踢出医疗补助计划时，他们会增加到这个数字中。

sentences.en: OK, so the first big effect is if you don't have insurance and the number of uninsured is about to really expand, you may be paying more for treatment.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以第一个重大影响是，如果你没有保险——而且无保险人数即将大幅增加——你可能要为治疗支付更多费用。

sentences.en: What's the second big effect?
sentences.zh: 第二个重大影响是什么？

sentences.en: The second biggest effect is that pharma companies are now going to charge a lot of money for vaccines and for treatments.
sentences.zh: 第二个最大的影响是，制药公司现在将对疫苗和治疗收取高额费用。

sentences.en: Pfizer and Moderna have both said that they'll charge somewhere between $80 and $130 for a vaccine dose.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞和莫德纳都表示，他们将对每剂疫苗收取80到130美元不等的费用。

sentences.en: The government was paying $30 per dose and we were getting it for free.
sentences.zh: 政府之前支付的是每剂30美元，而我们得到的是免费的。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: So that's a huge markup.
sentences.zh: 那可是巨大的加价。

sentences.en: That's a huge markup.
sentences.zh: 那可是巨大的加价。

sentences.en: But I thought that taxpayers themselves were the ones who paid for the development of this thing, right?
sentences.zh: 但我以为是纳税人自己支付了这些东西的研发费用，对吧？

sentences.en: Through that Operation Warp Speed that happened under the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 通过特朗普政府时期进行的“曲速行动”。

sentences.en: Like, why are these publicly paid for vaccines now going to make a lot of money for pharmaceutical companies?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些由公众买单的疫苗现在要为制药公司赚取巨额利润？

sentences.en: These agreements were made in the fog of war.
sentences.zh: 这些协议是在战争迷雾中达成的。

sentences.en: And my conversations with people who were involved say that the government did not get all that it could for its money.
sentences.zh: 我和相关人士的谈话表明，政府并没有从其投入的资金中获得应有的全部回报。

sentences.en: And they built in some things that made it very difficult for them to compel companies to do anything.
sentences.zh: 他们设定了一些条款，使得他们很难强迫公司做任何事情。

sentences.en: That means the companies are now free to charge whatever they want and they are free to develop anything new that they want.
sentences.zh: 这意味着公司现在可以自由地收取他们想要的任何费用，也可以自由地开发他们想要的任何新产品。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it all, again, just goes back to the market.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切，又回到了市场机制上。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So is this basically the government acknowledging that, yes, this will mean fewer people will have access to the vaccines and that's okay?
sentences.zh: 那么，这基本上是政府在承认：是的，这意味着更少的人能获得疫苗，而这没关系？

sentences.en: Because, you know, the vaccines are just not as important as they once were.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，疫苗已经不像以前那么重要了。

sentences.en: Because most people have gotten at least a few doses already.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数人已经至少接种了几剂疫苗。

sentences.en: They're not saying that.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有那样说。

sentences.en: What they're actually saying is that vaccines are really important and they're making sure that every insurance, every kind of insurance will have to cover vaccines.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是在说疫苗非常重要，并且他们正在确保每一种保险，每一种类型的保险都必须覆盖疫苗。

sentences.en: So if you have insurance, you won't really notice a difference.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有保险，你不会真正感觉到什么区别。

sentences.en: What is changing is that these manufacturers can now set the price for where they want it, sort of like they do for everything else.
sentences.zh: 改变的是，这些制造商现在可以随心所欲地设定价格，就像他们对待其他所有产品一样。

sentences.en: And then your insurance company is going to have to negotiate with them to figure out how they'll cover it.
sentences.zh: 然后你的保险公司将不得不与他们谈判，以确定他们将如何承保。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what's the third big effect?
sentences.zh: 那么第三个重大影响是什么？

sentences.en: The third big effect is something called Title 42, which is a policy implemented by the Trump administration way back in March 2020.
sentences.zh: 第三个重大影响是所谓的“第42条”（Title 42），这是特朗普政府早在2020年3月实施的一项政策。

sentences.en: And it allowed border patrol officers to send back migrants who were crossing the border from Mexico, sent them back to Mexico.
sentences.zh: 它允许边境巡逻人员将从墨西哥越境的移民遣返，把他们送回墨西哥。

sentences.en: And it was a public health order because the thinking was new people coming into the country increases COVID risk.
sentences.zh: 这是一项公共卫生令，因为当时的考虑是，进入该国的新人会增加新冠风险。

sentences.en: It's one of the ways in which we could contain the epidemic.
sentences.zh: 这是我们遏制疫情的方法之一。

sentences.en: Remember, in March 2020, things were pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 记住，在2020年3月，情况相当糟糕。

sentences.en: So we were trying everything.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时在尝试一切办法。

sentences.en: But what the Biden administration is saying now is if there is no public health emergency, then there's no need for Title 42 either.
sentences.zh: 但拜登政府现在所说的是，如果没有公共卫生紧急状态，那么也就没有必要再执行第42条了。

sentences.en: And so Title 42 will go away.
sentences.zh: 所以第42条将不复存在。

sentences.en: So the Biden administration is effectively now saying, you know, we're not in that public health emergency anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登政府实际上现在是在说，你知道，我们不再处于那种公共卫生紧急状态了。

sentences.en: We can no longer justify Title 42, the rule that allowed the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们无法再为第42条辩护，那项允许美国

sentences.en: to keep people out because it was a global pandemic.
sentences.zh: 因为全球大流行而将人们拒之门外的规则。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so what that means is that more people may now come to the border and seek to come into the United States because that rule is no longer in place.
sentences.zh: 这意味着现在可能会有更多人来到边境，寻求进入美国，因为那项规则不再生效了。

sentences.en: OK, so it sounds like with the end of the public health emergency, a few things are staying the same, but a lot of things are changing in pretty significant ways.
sentences.zh: 好的，听起来随着公共卫生紧急状态的结束，一些事情保持不变，但很多事情正在发生相当重大的变化。

sentences.en: But why is President Biden doing this?
sentences.zh: 但拜登总统为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: And why now?
sentences.zh: 而且为什么要现在做？

sentences.en: Well, why is because it's an acknowledgement that we are not in a public health emergency anymore.
sentences.zh: 嗯，之所以这么做，是因为这承认了我们不再处于公共卫生紧急状态中。

sentences.en: Why now?
sentences.zh: 为什么是现在？

sentences.en: The answer to that has a lot to do with politics.
sentences.zh: 这个问题的答案与政治有很大关系。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani and many others live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在NYTimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So, Apoorva, before the break, you said that the timing for the administration's decision to end the public health emergency is in part because of politics.
sentences.zh: 那么，阿普尔瓦，在休息之前，你说政府决定结束公共卫生紧急状态的时机部分是因为政治原因。

sentences.en: What are those politics?
sentences.zh: 那些政治因素是什么？

sentences.en: Well, this public health emergency was set to expire in April anyway.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这项公共卫生紧急状态本来就要在4月到期。

sentences.en: And the expectation from a lot of people was that it would either be allowed to finish then or that the Biden administration might extend it for a few more months.
sentences.zh: 许多人的预期是，它要么会到期结束，要么拜登政府可能会再延长几个月。

sentences.en: But certainly sometime this year, it would end.
sentences.zh: 但肯定在今年某个时候，它会结束。

sentences.en: Why this week?
sentences.zh: 为什么是这周？

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Speaker.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，议长先生。

sentences.en: Baker, today I rise to push for immediate and overwhelming passage of my legislation, H.R.
sentences.zh: 贝克，今天我站在这里，是为了推动立即且以压倒性多数通过我的立法，即H.R.

sentences.en: 382, the Pandemic is Over Act.
sentences.zh: 382号法案，《疫情结束法案》。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the House passed a bill called Pandemic is Over.
sentences.zh: 周二，众议院通过了一项名为《疫情结束》的法案。

sentences.en: As you know, Republicans have been saying now for many, many, many months that the pandemic is over.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，共和党人几个月来一直说疫情已经结束了。

sentences.en: This week, we are voting on several bills designed to do what we all in America have known for some time.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们正在投票表决几项旨在实现我们美国所有人都早已知晓之事的法案。

sentences.en: Americans have moved on from the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 美国人已经从疫情中走出来了。

sentences.en: Georgians in my district went back to work and back to school over two years ago.
sentences.zh: 我选区的佐治亚州人在两年多前就回到了工作岗位和学校。

sentences.en: Emergency executive authority should be limited and only for extraordinary circumstances.
sentences.zh: 紧急行政权力应该受到限制，且仅用于特殊情况。

sentences.en: And this is no longer an extraordinary circumstance.
sentences.zh: 而这已不再是特殊情况。

sentences.en: And this bill was meant to end the public health emergency the second it was signed into law.
sentences.zh: 这项法案旨在一旦签署成为法律，就立即结束公共卫生紧急状态。

sentences.en: The pandemic is over.
sentences.zh: 疫情已经结束。

sentences.en: It's a loud and clear message to President Biden.
sentences.zh: 这对拜登总统来说是一个明确无误的信号。

sentences.en: The American people are tired of living in a perpetual state of emergency.
sentences.zh: 美国人民已经厌倦了长期处于紧急状态的生活。

sentences.en: And it's long overdue for Congress to take back the authorities granted under Article 1 of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 国会早该收回宪法第一条所赋予的权力了。

sentences.en: Now, that was probably never going to happen because the Senate wouldn't have passed it.
sentences.zh: 当然，这大概永远不会发生，因为参议院不会通过它。

sentences.en: But this was their way of saying we think the pandemic is over.
sentences.zh: 但这正是他们表达“我们认为疫情已经结束”的一种方式。

sentences.en: But what it would have meant is that everything that the public health emergency put into place would have ended immediately the second this became law.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着公共卫生紧急状态下实施的一切措施，都会在法律生效的那一刻立即终止。

sentences.en: The Biden administration has always said they would give at least 60 days warning for everything to unwind because they put so many complicated things into place.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府一直表示，他们会至少提前60天发出预警，以便撤销各项措施，因为他们实施了太多复杂的政策。

sentences.en: The system needs time to undo all of those things.
sentences.zh: 系统需要时间来撤销所有这些措施。

sentences.en: And so this was the Biden administration's way of saying we agree with you.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是拜登政府表达“我们同意你们的看法”的方式。

sentences.en: The pandemic is over, but we're going to do this on our terMs.
sentences.zh: 疫情确实结束了，但我们要按自己的节奏来处理。

sentences.en: So the decision to do this now was not based purely on some public health calculation about COVID.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在做出这个决定并非完全基于某种关于新冠的公共卫生计算。

sentences.en: Well, there's no real public health metric that these things can be based on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些措施并没有真正的公共卫生指标作为依据。

sentences.en: But the administration has been saying for quite a long time now that we are not in the same state of crisis that we were in.
sentences.zh: 但政府很长一段时间以来一直在说，我们已经不再处于过去那种危机状态了。

sentences.en: And the numbers do show that, you know, we did not have anywhere near the kind of deaths or even hospitalizations that we saw the previous two winters.
sentences.zh: 数据也确实显示，你看，我们的死亡人数甚至住院人数都远不及前两个冬天。

sentences.en: And we weren't taking precautions this year.
sentences.zh: 而且我们今年也没有采取什么预防措施。

sentences.en: So this is really an acknowledgement of something that the administration and a lot of experts have been saying for quite a while, which is this is a new phase.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是对政府和许多专家早已指出的事实的一种认可，那就是我们进入了一个新阶段。

sentences.en: But that said, I do want to note that we are still seeing somewhere around 500 deaths a day.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，我还是要指出，我们每天仍有大约500人死亡。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I mean, these are not trivial numbers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些数字绝非微不足道。

sentences.en: You know, they feel like a lot less because they are a lot less than the previous years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们让人感觉少了很多，因为相比往年确实少了很多。

sentences.en: But this is still a pretty high level of damage that COVID is able to inflict.
sentences.zh: 但新冠病毒仍能造成相当严重的破坏。

sentences.en: Even if most people feel like this is done, the virus is not done with us.
sentences.zh: 即使大多数人觉得疫情已经结束，病毒却并没有放过我们。

sentences.en: Does any of this change the way we should be thinking about how we approach COVID?
sentences.zh: 这一切是否改变了我们看待新冠的方式？

sentences.en: Like as individuals?
sentences.zh: 比如作为个人？

sentences.en: What should be my COVID hygiene practices, if you will?
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我的新冠卫生习惯应该是什么样的？

sentences.en: How you feel about the pandemic and what you do really depends on your risk level and your risk tolerance.
sentences.zh: 你对疫情的感受以及你的行为，实际上取决于你的风险水平和风险承受能力。

sentences.en: If you are over 65, if you're immunocompromised, if you're pregnant, if you have a baby under one and you want to protect that baby, the virus is still very much a threat.
sentences.zh: 如果你超过65岁，如果你免疫功能低下，如果你怀孕了，或者你有一个不到一岁的婴儿并想保护他，那么病毒仍然是一个巨大的威胁。

sentences.en: And those people should still continue to mask everywhere they can to get their vaccine doses on time and to protect themselves every way they can.
sentences.zh: 这些人仍应尽可能在任何地方佩戴口罩，按时接种疫苗，并尽一切可能保护自己。

sentences.en: For everybody else, really, it's a matter of personal choice now because the government is saying we're no longer thinking this is an emergency.
sentences.zh: 对于其他人来说，这确实成了个人选择的问题，因为政府已经表示不再认为这是紧急状态了。

sentences.en: You make the decision.
sentences.zh: 由你自己决定。

sentences.en: So it sounds like you're saying I don't need to get a booster anymore.
sentences.zh: 听起来你是说我不需要再打加强针了。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm a healthy person.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我是一个健康的人。

sentences.en: I'm done with boosters.
sentences.zh: 我不需要再打加强针了。

sentences.en: It seems that way from this winter.
sentences.zh: 从这个冬天的情况来看，似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: You know, only about 16 percent of the population got the bivalent booster.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只有大约16%的人口接种了二价加强针。

sentences.en: And yet this winter, we didn't see anywhere near the kind of deaths we saw the last two winters.
sentences.zh: 然而这个冬天，我们并没有看到像过去两个冬天那样的死亡人数。

sentences.en: Even this winter, the people who are in the hospitals are older adults who are most at risk from any respiratory disease.
sentences.zh: 即使在这个冬天，住院的人也主要是老年人，他们是任何呼吸道疾病的高危人群。

sentences.en: Having said that, the FDA has said they would like to go to a system where everybody would get an annual shot, kind of like we do for the flu.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，FDA表示他们希望转向一种系统，即每个人每年都接种一次疫苗，就像我们接种流感疫苗一样。

sentences.en: So then can we just start treating this thing like the flu?
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在可以开始把它当作流感来对待了吗？

sentences.en: Is COVID the flu basically at this point?
sentences.zh: 新冠在这一点上基本上就是流感吗？

sentences.en: No, it's not the flu.
sentences.zh: 不，它不是流感。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an endemic virus like the flu in the sense that we're going to live with this forever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是一种像流感一样的流行性病毒，因为我们将永远与它共存。

sentences.en: But we don't know it anywhere near as well as we know the flu.
sentences.zh: 但我们对它的了解远不及对流感的了解。

sentences.en: Flu is a very old friend, an old enemy.
sentences.zh: 流感是一个非常熟悉的朋友，也是一个老对手。

sentences.en: And COVID is still such a mystery to us.
sentences.zh: 而新冠对我们来说仍然是一个谜。

sentences.en: It's way more contagious.
sentences.zh: 它的传染性强得多。

sentences.en: It's way more deadly.
sentences.zh: 它的致命性也强得多。

sentences.en: And we really have no idea about its seasonality.
sentences.zh: 而且我们对它的季节性一无所知。

sentences.en: We know, for example, that, okay, every winter we'll probably see a wave of some size.
sentences.zh: 例如我们知道，好吧，每个冬天我们可能会看到一定规模的疫情浪潮。

sentences.en: But we don't know when else in the year it might come.
sentences.zh: 但我们不知道它在一年中的其他时候何时会出现。

sentences.en: We don't know how big it will be.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道规模会有多大。

sentences.en: We don't know how often it will change, which new variant will come our way.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道它会多久变异一次，也不知道会有什么新变种出现。

sentences.en: There's just so many unanswered things about this virus that are not the case for flu.
sentences.zh: 关于这种病毒，有太多未解之谜，而流感则不然。

sentences.en: That is not the answer I was hoping for.
sentences.zh: 那不是我希望得到的答案。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems to kind of behave in the same way roughly, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它看起来表现得大致相同，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay, so we don't know what season it comes in.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们不知道它在什么季节出现。

sentences.en: But it's just, it's not changing our lives and turning them upside down in the way that it once was.
sentences.zh: 但它只是，它不再像以前那样改变我们的生活，把我们的生活搞得天翻地覆了。

sentences.en: At the moment.
sentences.zh: 目前是这样。

sentences.en: I really hesitate to draw conclusions about what this virus is doing because it has thrown so many surprises at us.
sentences.zh: 我真的不敢对这种病毒的行为下结论，因为它给了我们太多的意外。

sentences.en: It could still come up with a new variant that gets around the vaccines.
sentences.zh: 它仍可能出现一种能绕过疫苗的新变种。

sentences.en: We may all still need to go get another booster.
sentences.zh: 我们可能仍需要去打另一针加强针。

sentences.en: We may need new drugs.
sentences.zh: 我们可能需要新的药物。

sentences.en: We are not fully out of the woods.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有完全脱离险境。

sentences.en: Do you think it will ever get predictable in the way that the flu is?
sentences.zh: 你认为它会变得像流感那样可以预测吗？

sentences.en: Or are we seriously just living with this unpredictable thing forever?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们真的要永远和这种不可预测的东西生活在一起？

sentences.en: That's the hope.
sentences.zh: 这就是希望所在。

sentences.en: We will understand when this virus comes around.
sentences.zh: 我们将了解这种病毒何时会出现。

sentences.en: You know, it hasn't been long enough.
sentences.zh: 你知道，时间还不够长。

sentences.en: We've only been in this for three years.
sentences.zh: 我们才经历了三年。

sentences.en: And the previous two years, we didn't see other respiratory viruses.
sentences.zh: 而在前两年，我们没有看到其他呼吸道病毒。

sentences.en: This year we had RSV, we had flu, we had COVID.
sentences.zh: 今年我们有了RSV、流感和新冠。

sentences.en: And we don't know how those viruses really play with each other yet, how they will affect each other's seasonality.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道这些病毒之间是如何相互作用的，也不知道它们将如何影响彼此的季节性。

sentences.en: So we need at least another year or a couple more years to see what this virus does at different parts of the year.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要至少再过一年或几年，才能观察这种病毒在一年中不同时期的表现。

sentences.en: Apoeva, the last time we did an episode together, I asked you if COVID was a road trip from the East Coast to the West Coast, where were we in that journey?
sentences.zh: Apoeva，上次我们一起做节目时，我问你如果新冠是从东海岸到西海岸的公路旅行，我们现在处于旅程的什么位置？

sentences.en: And I think at the time, some point last year, you said somewhere in the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 我想当时，去年某个时候，你说是在中西部某处。

sentences.en: Where are we on the journey?
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于旅程的什么位置？

sentences.en: How close are we to San Francisco?
sentences.zh: 我们离旧金山还有多远？

sentences.en: We're closer, but San Francisco may never have been the destination.
sentences.zh: 我们更近了，但旧金山可能从来都不是目的地。

sentences.en: If we thought that we were going to reach heart immunity and be rid of this virus, San Francisco was never in the cards.
sentences.zh: 如果我们以为能达到群体免疫并摆脱这种病毒，那旧金山从来就不在计划之内。

sentences.en: The GPS was always set to Denver.
sentences.zh: GPS一直设定的目的地是丹佛。

sentences.en: We just thought we were headed to San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们只是以为我们要去旧金山。

sentences.en: Apoeva, thank you.
sentences.zh: Apoeva，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的消息。

sentences.en: This resolution is not about engaging in a tit-for-tat with my colleagues on the other side of the aisle.
sentences.zh: 这项决议并非为了与我党派对立面的同事进行针锋相对的争斗。

sentences.en: This is about keeping someone with a long record of anti-Semitic and anti-Israel bias off the Foreign Affairs Committee, which needs objective emissaries for our foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 这是为了阻止一个长期有反犹太和反以色列偏见记录的人进入外交事务委员会，该委员会需要客观的外交政策使者。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Republican-led House passed a resolution to oust Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota
sentences.zh: 周四，共和党领导的众议院通过了一项决议，将明尼苏达州众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔（Ilhan Omar）

sentences.en: from the Foreign Affairs Committee over her past comments about Israel that were condemned as anti-Semitic.
sentences.zh: 逐出外交事务委员会，原因在于她过去关于以色列的言论被谴责为反犹太主义。

sentences.en: There is an idea out there that I do not have objective decision-making because of who I am, where I come from, and my perspective.
sentences.zh: 有一种观点认为，由于我的身份、出身和视角，我无法做出客观的决策。

sentences.en: But I reject that.
sentences.zh: 但我拒绝接受这种说法。

sentences.en: We say there is nothing objective about policymaking.
sentences.zh: 我们认为决策制定本身就没有绝对的客观性。

sentences.en: We all inject our perspective, our point of views, our lived experiences, and the voices of our constituents.
sentences.zh: 我们都注入了自己的视角、观点、生活经历以及选民的声音。

sentences.en: That's what democracy is about.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主的意义所在。

sentences.en: The move settled a partisan score in the House that had been festering since 2021 when Democrats stripped Republicans of their committee assignments
sentences.zh: 此举解决了众议院内自2021年以来一直积压的党派恩怨，当时民主党人剥夺了共和党人的委员会席位，

sentences.en: in response to social media posts that endorsed violence against Democrats.
sentences.zh: 以回应他们支持针对民主党人暴力的社交媒体帖子。

sentences.en: And the U.S.
sentences.zh: 此外，美国

sentences.en: announced it would increase its military presence in the Philippines to what will be the largest U.S.
sentences.zh: 宣布将增加在菲律宾的军事存在，这将是美国

sentences.en: presence there in 30 years.
sentences.zh: 30年来在那里最大的军事存在。

sentences.en: The plan allows Washington to station military equipment and build facilities in nine locations across the country.
sentences.zh: 该计划允许华盛顿在全国九个地点驻扎军事装备并建造设施。

sentences.en: Some of the locations were bases that it had already been using.
sentences.zh: 其中一些地点是它已经在使用中的基地。

sentences.en: The deal comes as Washington tries to reaffirm its influence in the region and to counter what it sees as aggression from China.
sentences.zh: 此项协议达成之际，华盛顿正试图重申其在该地区的影响力，并对抗它所认为的来自中国的侵略。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Michael Simon Johnson, Shannon Lin, and Jessica Chung.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Michael Simon Johnson、Shannon Lin和Jessica Chung制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lexi Diao and Paige Cowett with help from M.J.

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《Metro》节目中，我和Sarah Koenig将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
